GETTING STARTED

Start with a test you can explain.

Short answer

Intents is a free, open-source Mac workbench for Apple Foundation Models. Start with one prompt, a concrete expectation, and a saved response. Then add cases that expose failures.

Choose a build

Released download: Intents 1.5.2

Intents was previously named Foundation Evals. The released app includes prompt suites, scoring, traces, saved comparisons, Review, Batch runs, JSON exports, and authenticated local MCP access.

Download for macOS · v1.5.2 · Release notes and checksums

brew install --cask coryparrry/tap/intents

Open Intents-1.5.2-macOS-arm64.dmg, drag Intents to Applications, eject the disk image, and open the app. Follow the v1.5.2 instructions for this interface.

Development source: Intents

Build source to develop the app or try changes that have not shipped. Review and Batch runs are also available in the released 1.5.2 app. Check published releases for any later download.

With Xcode 27 and its command-line tools selected, clone the repository and run the project’s build script:

git clone https://github.com/coryparrry/Intents.git
cd Intents
./script/build_and_run.sh

The script builds and opens dist/Intents.app. Read the source build instructions and current user guide.

Check model readiness

Requires macOS 27 or later. The default on-device provider needs an Apple Intelligence–capable Apple silicon Mac, Apple Intelligence enabled, and its model downloaded. Ordinary on-device suites do not need Xcode. Source builds and Mac App Intent tests require Xcode 27.

Compatible Core AI models and custom HTTP providers have their own requirements. Remote providers and judges use their configured services. Optional Private Cloud Compute uses Apple’s service; tools can disclose the content needed for their calls. See data and troubleshooting.

Run your first case

In the released app, select Model evaluations → New Suite → Blank suite → Create suite, then open Cases and Setup → Scoring.

  1. Name the case “Capital answer”. Enter the prompt Reply with only the capital of France and expected text Paris.
  2. Choose Exact text to check the whole answer. Choose Contains text if extra words are allowed. Start with one repetition and no tools.
  3. Check that the model is ready, run the suite, and open its saved report and workflow trace. The current getting-started guide explains the app controls.

Read and compare results

Inspect the actual answer alongside the score. A pass means the response met your chosen scoring rule. Traces help explain measured stages and tool activity. Change one instruction, rerun the same cases, and compare the saved runs.

Add a formatting failure, an ambiguous request, and a changed-preference case. Use repetitions to inspect variation. Small examples are not model benchmarks and do not establish statistical certainty. In the released app, Review records human verdicts and verified regression cases; Batch runs retains frozen datasets and resumable jobs.

Testing your app’s actions

Mac App Intent tests in development source reads a built Mac app’s compiled metadata and accepts explicit JSON inputs and expected returned values. The generated AppIntentsTesting UI-test runner needs Xcode 27+, macOS 27+, a normally installed and registered app, and matching development-team signatures. This is an unshipped source workflow; live runner reliability is not qualified and Siri is not verified.

Help improve a failure case

When reporting an issue, include your release or source commit, macOS and model, a minimal synthetic prompt, scoring rule, expected result, and actual response. Review exports for private content before attaching them. A reproducible case, documentation correction, or focused patch helps others test the same behavior. The source uses the MIT licence.

Version facts checked 26 October 2026. The homepage’s HTML/CSS examples use a recorded 17 September evaluation and an illustrative source-only Mac App Intent contract. They are browser recreations, not live model or App Intent execution. Example scores are not model benchmarks.
